entries.sense_en: to do small naughty things that cause trouble

synonyms.nuance: Wider and more serious: can mean real problems with police, school or money, not just playful naughtiness.
synonyms.example: He got into trouble at school.

synonyms.nuance: Neutral, slightly formal; describes bad behavior without the playful, childlike tone of mischief.
Deliberately fooling someone for fun; mischief need not involve tricking anyone.
synonyms.example: They played tricks on their teacher.

entries.tip_ko: 강세는 첫 음절 MIS-에 있어요. 형용사 mischievous도 [MIS-chi-vəs] 3음절이지 'mis-CHEE-vi-ous'가 아니에요.

entries.sense_en: a small dried grape used in baking

synonyms.nuance: A larger dried grape; the everyday American word for any dried grape.
A pale, golden dried grape; mostly British usage.

entries.tip_ko: current(현재의, 흐름)와 발음이 똑같아요. 철자로만 구별합니다.

entries.sense_en: badly behaved and not doing what you are told (usually of a child)

synonyms.nuance: Playful and fond of harmless tricks; often said with a smile, less disapproving.
Stresses refusing to obey orders; more formal and serious.
Plain and general; naughty is the softer word used for children.

entries.tip_ko: 어른에게 쓰면 '야한'이라는 뜻이 될 수 있으니 주로 아이나 동물에게 쓰세요.

entries.sense_en: pushed through a very narrow space with difficulty

synonyms.nuance: Moving quickly and easily, often unnoticed; no sense of tightness.
synonyms.example: She slipped out of the room.

synonyms.nuance: Twisting the body from side to side to get through or free.
Forcing too much into a space; usually about packing things, not moving yourself.

entries.sense_en: used to show a surprising, unwelcome meeting: he met, of all people, …

synonyms.nuance: Modern, everyday way to stress surprise about who it was.
synonyms.example: And he met Mr. McGregor, of all people!

synonyms.nuance: Plain phrasal verb for an unplanned meeting; carries no dramatic surprise by itself.
synonyms.example: I ran into my boss at the store.

entries.modern: "And who did he run into? Mr. McGregor!"
entries.tip_ko: 의문문처럼 보이지만 질문이 아니라 놀람을 강조하는 옛 문어체 표현이에요.

entries.sense_en: a garden tool with a long handle and a row of metal teeth

synonyms.nuance: Has a flat blade, used for cutting weeds and breaking soil, not for gathering leaves.
Long handle with two or three large prongs for lifting hay.

entries.sense_en: extremely, very badly

synonyms.nuance: The most common everyday equivalent; neutral in tone.
Informal intensifier, can be used with good things too.
Old-fashioned and very British; sounds upper-class today.

entries.sense_en: in the middle of; surrounded by

synonyms.nuance: Same meaning; the normal form, especially in American English. Amongst sounds British or literary.
Usually for two separate things, or clearly separate points.
Formal; often for being in the middle of events or noise.

entries.sense_en: to stop hoping and believe you will surely be caught or die

synonyms.nuance: Everyday modern phrase; less dramatic.
One formal verb; stresses the painful feeling of having no hope.

entries.modern: "Peter thought it was all over for him."
entries.tip_ko: give up(포기하다)이나 give oneself up(자수하다)과 헷갈리기 쉬워요. 여기서는 for lost가 붙어 '끝장났다고 여기다'입니다.

entries.sense_en: let tears fall from your eyes; cried

synonyms.nuance: Literary verb for crying, often quietly and for a long time.
The ordinary everyday word.
Crying loudly with short breaths; the body shakes.

entries.tip_ko: tool-shed의 shed(창고, 명사)와는 전혀 다른 단어예요.

entries.sense_en: begged someone very strongly and emotionally to do something

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; can sound less dignified or desperate.
Strongly advise or push someone; less emotional pleading.
Often used with 'with' or 'for'; suggests a serious, emotional appeal.
synonyms.example: She pleaded with him to listen.

entries.sense_en: to make a big physical effort; try hard

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrase; can be mental or physical.
synonyms.example: Make an effort to be on time.

synonyms.nuance: Stresses difficulty and fighting against something.
Pushing hard enough to risk hurting yourself.

entries.tip_ko: exert는 [이그저트]처럼 x를 [gz]로 발음하고, 강세는 뒤에 있어요.

entries.sense_en: a round tool with a wire net, used to separate small bits from large ones

synonyms.nuance: Mainly for separating liquid from food, like pasta water or tea leaves.
A bowl with holes for draining washed vegetables or pasta.
synonyms.example: Drain the pasta in a colander.

entries.tip_ko: sieve는 ie 철자와 달리 [시-브]처럼 길게 읽지 않고, give와 같은 짧은 모음 /ɪ/로 [시v]라고 읽어요.

entries.sense_en: twisted and turned the body quickly to get free

synonyms.nuance: Twisting from discomfort, pain or embarrassment, not only to escape.
Small, quick side-to-side movements, often playful.
Violent twisting, usually from great pain.

entries.sense_en: soon; after a short time

synonyms.nuance: Plain everyday word for 'not long after'.
Slightly formal; common in announcements.
Means 'now'; modern American 'presently' often has this meaning instead.

entries.tip_ko: 오늘날 미국 영어에서 presently는 주로 '현재'라는 뜻이라 헷갈리기 쉬워요. 옛 이야기에서는 '곧'입니다.

entries.sense_en: very quickly; almost at once

synonyms.nuance: Stresses starting immediately, not how fast something is done.
Informal and vivid; extremely fast, like lightning.
synonyms.example: He was gone in a flash.

entries.sense_en: knocking something over by accident

synonyms.nuance: The everyday phrasal verb for this physical meaning.
synonyms.example: The cat knocked over a glass.

synonyms.nuance: Suggests tilting until it falls; can happen slowly.
More formal; often for vehicles or furniture turned upside down.

entries.tip_ko: 보통 '속상하게 하다'로 알지만 여기서는 물건을 '엎다'라는 원래 뜻이에요.

entries.sense_en: breathing fast and hard after running or effort

synonyms.nuance: One adjective; can also describe excitement, not only tiredness.
Describes the action: short, quick, noisy breaths, like a dog.

entries.sense_en: not know at all

synonyms.nuance: The common everyday form; same meaning, less emphatic.
synonyms.example: I have no idea where he is.

synonyms.nuance: Informal; can suggest someone is ignorant or incompetent.
synonyms.example: He doesn't have a clue about cars.

synonyms.nuance: Same strong emphasis; a little old-fashioned or British.

entries.sense_en: slightly wet, often in an unpleasant way

synonyms.nuance: Slightly wet in a pleasant or neutral way, e.g. cake or skin.
Covered in or full of water; stronger than damp.
Only for air or weather full of moisture.

entries.sense_en: confused because you cannot understand or solve something

synonyms.nuance: General and common; can also mean mentally mixed up.
Stronger: completely unable to understand.
Confused and lost, often by too many things at once.

entries.sense_en: made a small, sudden movement

synonyms.nuance: A bigger, sharper sudden movement.
A quick light movement, often deliberate, like a tail or finger.
Continuous small shaking, usually from fear or cold.

entries.sense_en: a garden tool with a long handle and flat blade, used to remove weeds

synonyms.nuance: Has a row of teeth for gathering leaves or smoothing soil.
A flat blade you push into the ground to dig.
synonyms.example: dig a hole with a spade

synonyms.nuance: A small hand tool for planting.

entries.sense_en: ran quickly with short little steps, like a small frightened animal

synonyms.nuance: The common modern word: quick short steps, often in a hurry or fear.
Quick, short steps, often sideways, like a crab.
One quick run; no sense of small steps or fear.

entries.sense_en: looked quickly and secretly, trying not to be seen

synonyms.nuance: Very close; the more common modern word for a quick secret look.
A quick look, but not secret.
Looking hard and long because it is hard to see.

entries.sense_en: suddenly see someone for a short moment

synonyms.nuance: Informal; notice something, often after looking for it.
synonyms.example: I spotted her in the crowd.

synonyms.nuance: See only partly or very briefly.
synonyms.example: We glimpsed the sea from the train.

synonyms.nuance: Become aware of; not necessarily by seeing.

entries.sense_en: a figure dressed in old clothes, put in a field to frighten birds away

synonyms.nuance: Any human-shaped model, e.g. in a shop or for testing.
Today mostly figurative: a weak argument made up to be easily defeated.

entries.sense_en: dropped down heavily and loosely because he was so tired

synonyms.nuance: Falling because of illness or exhaustion; more serious.
Sitting or falling heavily with the body bent, often sadly.
Sitting or dropping down casually, with a light sound.
synonyms.example: He plopped down on the sofa.

entries.tip_ko: flop은 '(영화 등이) 쫄딱 망하다'라는 뜻으로도 자주 쓰여요.

entries.sense_en: a period of two weeks

synonyms.nuance: The normal American way to say it; fortnight is mainly British.
synonyms.example: I'll be away for two weeks.

synonyms.nuance: Adjective for 'every two weeks' (confusingly, also 'twice a week').

entries.sense_en: an amount of medicine taken at one time

synonyms.nuance: The correct amount and how often to take it; technical, on labels.
synonyms.example: Check the dosage on the label.

synonyms.nuance: Just the amount one spoon holds; not only medicine.

entries.tip_ko: dose는 [도우스]로, s를 [z]로 발음하지 마세요 (doze '졸다'와 다른 단어).
